cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, gathers the whole congregation of Israel. EVERYBODY. He's got things the LORD has commanded them to do.

cards.question: Moses starts with the week. Six days of work, and then the seventh day is a holy day, a Sabbath of complete ___ to the LORD.

cards.text: And this is serious, friend. Whoever does any work on that day must be put to death.

cards.question: On the Sabbath, the people can still light a fire in their homes.

cards.text: Then Moses moves on to something new. The LORD has commanded an offering.

cards.question: Moses tells the people who should bring this offering to the LORD. Who is it?

answers.text: Every man twenty years or older

cards.text: Then comes a long list of materials, from gold, silver and bronze all the way down to onyx stones and gemstones. Back on the Millers' counter, ONE new cookie cutter was a big day, and this list would've knocked me right off the counter.

cards.question: The LORD wants more than materials. Who does Moses call to come and make everything the LORD has commanded?

cards.text: And they're making EVERYTHING: the tabernacle and all its furnishings, down to the tent pegs and ropes, plus the holy garments for Aaron the priest and his sons.
Then the whole congregation of Israel walks away from Moses. Friend, I've seen a room clear out after a big meeting, and I KNOW how that usually goes.

cards.question: After they leave Moses, the people whose hearts are stirred come back with an offering to the LORD.

cards.text: And here they come, men and women both, everyone with a willing heart. And some of them are bringing gold.

cards.question: What kind of gold do the men and women bring to the LORD?

cards.text: Whoever has yarn, linen, goat hair, ram skins or leather brings it. Whoever has silver, bronze or acacia wood brings that too.

cards.question: The skilled women spin yarn, linen and goat hair with their own hands and bring what they've spun.
The ___ bring the onyx stones and gemstones for the ephod and breastpiece, plus spices and olive oil.
All the men and women whose hearts prompted them bring a ___ offering to the LORD.

cards.text: Then Moses says the LORD has called Bezalel son of Uri, of the tribe of Judah, by NAME. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer just hoping somebody would remember mine.

cards.question: The LORD has filled Bezalel with the ___ of God, along with skill, ability and knowledge.

cards.text: Bezalel can design in gold, silver and bronze, cut gemstones and carve wood. Me, I press dough, and that's the WHOLE résumé.
The LORD has also gifted Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan. Bezalel's got a partner, and friend, the only partner I had in the junk drawer was a twist tie that never helped with ANYTHING.

cards.question: The LORD gives both Bezalel and Oholiab the ability to ___ others.
The LORD fills Bezalel and Oholiab with skill to work as embroiderers and weavers too.

cards.text: So Moses says it plainly: Bezalel, Oholiab and every skilled person are to carry out everything the LORD has commanded. Then he summons them all.

cards.question: The workers Moses summons are people whose hearts stirred them to come and do the work.

cards.text: Moses hands the craftsmen all the contributions the Israelites brought, and the work begins. But the people still aren't finished.

cards.question: How often do the people keep bringing freewill offerings for the sanctuary?
With offerings still coming in every morning, what do all the skilled craftsmen working on the sanctuary do?

answers.text: They leave their work to talk to Moses
They ask for more gold and silver
They call for more workers to help

cards.question: The craftsmen tell Moses the people are bringing more than enough for the work the LORD commanded.

cards.text: Moses gives an order, and they send a proclamation all through the camp. Friend, the last big announcement I ever heard came from the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, and it was just them SWEARING they still had a little charge left.

cards.question: What does the proclamation throughout the camp tell the men and women?

answers.text: No one should make any more offerings
Everyone should bring twice as much
Only the leaders should bring more

cards.text: So the people are held back from bringing more. Friend, have you EVER heard of a fundraiser begging people to STOP giving?
What they already have is more than enough to do all the work. Hold on to your aprons, friend, because this story's not done.
